title.narrative: Strengthening cocoa and beekeeping production to increase living incomes and mitigate climate change

description.narrative: Coffee-growing communities in the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta, Colombia, face persistent social, economic, and environmental challenges. Smallholder farmers – many cultivating one to two hectares – are increasingly affected by climate change, fluctuating market prices, and reliance on coffee monocropping. These pressures result in unstable incomes that fall short of a living income, particularly between harvest periods, and contribute to youth migration, gender inequality, and reduced resilience of rural livelihoods. Environmental risks such as biodiversity loss, soil degradation, and climate vulnerability further threaten the long-term sustainability of the coffee value chain.This project addresses these challenges through an integrated approach that strengthens cocoa and beekeeping production alongside organic coffee farming. By promoting agroforestry systems, climate-resilient practices, and landscape restoration, the project aims to diversify incomes while conserving ecosystems. The initiative is implemented through a partnership between a Fairtrade Original B.V. (a Dutch buyer), La Red Ecolsierra (a local producer cooperative), and Corporación Paisajes Rurales (a Colombian environmental NGO) ensuring alignment between market requirements, local capacities, and environmental sustainability.The primary beneficiaries are 208 smallholder farming families, of whom 108 families will receive direct support through the establishment or improvement of cocoa agroforestry systems and 100 families through beekeeping activities. At least 25% of the beneficiaries are women, with a strong focus on engaging youth to enhance intergenerational continuity. Indirect beneficiaries include additional farming households, local service providers, and community stakeholders involved in training, restoration, and value-chain development.The envisioned impact of the project is a measurable increase in household incomes, reduced dependence on a single crop, and improved year-round income stability. Environmentally, the project will contribute to biodiversity conservation, climate adaptation, and deforestation-free production. Socially, it will strengthen local capacities, promote gender inclusion, reduce the risk of youth outmigration, and support compliance with international sustainability and due diligence standards. Overall, the project aims to build a more resilient, inclusive, and sustainable supply chain that benefits both producers and markets.
